question: Driving at a constant speed, Sharon usually takes \(180\) minutes to drive from her house to her mother’s house. One day Sharon begins the drive at her usual speed, but after driving \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) of the way, she hits a bad snowstorm and reduces her speed by \(20\) miles per hour. This time the trip takes her a total of \(276\) minutes. How many miles is the drive from Sharon’s house to her mother’s house?
solution:
The first third of the trip is driven at Sharon's usual speed, so it still takes \(180/3=60\) minutes. The remaining two thirds therefore takes
\[
276-60=216\text{ minutes}=\frac{18}{5}\text{ hours}.
\]
Let \(r\) be her usual speed in miles per hour. Normally the whole trip takes \(3\) hours, so the last two thirds would take \(2\) hours and cover \(2r\) miles. During the storm, she covers that same distance at \(r-20\) miles per hour. Hence
\[
2r=\frac{18}{5}(r-20).
\]
Multiplying by \(5\) and solving gives
\[
10r=18r-360,
\qquad 8r=360,
\qquad r=45.
\]
The full distance is therefore \(3\cdot45=\boxed{135}\) miles, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
